1.name: Wu Xin
1.about: One of the most prominent prospects to emerge from China in recent years, Wu enters the season at the top of the preseason board. The skilled 6'11" big brings an appealing combination of shooting touch, passing feel and interior scoring, giving him a versatile offensive foundation and making him an early candidate to establish himself as the class's top prospect.

2.name: Nathan Essome
2.about: Playing professionally with the New Zealand Breakers has given Essome an early opportunity to showcase his explosive first step, long 6'9" wingspan and ability to create from either guard spot. The French prospect enters the year firmly in the No. 1 pick conversation, with his two-way tools and attacking ability giving him one of the most intriguing ceilings in the class.

3.name: Tate Woods
3.about: The nation's No. 1 recruit, Woods arrives at Texas as one of the most anticipated freshmen in the class. At 6'10" with a 7'2" wingspan, his ability to create pull-up jumpers, attack mismatches and handle scoring responsibilities from the perimeter gives him a rare offensive profile and significant upside entering his first college season.

4.name: Jokūbas Kanapinskas
4.about: One of the most highly recruited international prospects entering college basketball, Kanapinskas arrives at Vanderbilt with significant expectations. The 6'8" Lithuanian playmaker brings advanced passing instincts, perimeter shooting and pick-and-roll feel, with his combination of size and offensive creativity giving Vanderbilt a versatile centerpiece to build its offense around.

5.name: Ishaan Cooper
5.about: An explosive five-star freshman from the Bahamas, Cooper arrives at Kansas with an unusual blend of power, length and playmaking for a 6'4" guard. He thrives attacking the paint, creating through contact and finding teammates once the defense collapses. His elite athletic tools give him plenty of avenues to impact games while his perimeter game continues developing.

6.name: K'yeon Moore
6.about: One of Syracuse’s highest-profile incoming freshmen, Moore arrives as a five-star recruit with the scoring talent to make an immediate impact. He creates separation off the bounce, is comfortable rising into pull-ups and can punish defenders who crowd his jumper. His advanced scoring package gives him a strong foundation to emerge as a top prospect early in the season.

7.name: Tai Scott
7.about: After starring as a freshman at Auburn, Scott surprised many by returning for his sophomore season rather than entering the NBA Draft. His pull-up shooting, change of pace and advanced shot creation already made him one of college basketball's most dynamic guards, and he enters year two with an opportunity to further elevate his stock near the top of the class.

8.name: Kendall Williams
8.about: BYU landed a major frontcourt talent in five-star recruit Williams, whose physical tools immediately separate him from most players in the class. His powerful 238-pound frame, 7'2" wingspan and elite explosiveness complement his rebounding and interior scoring, giving him the tools to make an immediate impact around the basket on both ends.

9.name: Damir Thompson
9.about: After playing a complementary role at Kentucky as a freshman, Thompson transferred to Arizona State for the opportunity to become a featured creator. Scouts love his 6'7" frame, 6'11" wingspan and ability to legitimately play point guard, giving him an enticing combination of positional size, creation and versatility entering his sophomore season.

10.name: Evan Williams
10.about: A top-three recruit in the nation, Williams arrives at Villanova widely regarded as the best defender in the class. His 6'5" frame, 6'11" wingspan, athleticism and instincts give him the tools to overwhelm opposing guards at the point of attack, while his developing creation ability provides intriguing upside as a big lead guard.
